rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis-B clinical and public-health management
rows.verified: UKHSA guidance covers the diagnosis, prevention and treatment of hepatitis B.

rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis-B clinical and public-health management
rows.verified: Hepatitis B virus replicates in the liver and can cause acute or chronic infection.

rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis-B clinical and public-health management
rows.verified: Chronic hepatitis B can cause severe liver damage, cirrhosis, liver failure and cancer.

rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis-B clinical and public-health management
rows.verified: Hepatitis B is vaccine preventable.

rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis-B clinical and public-health management
rows.verified: The virus can be transmitted through infected blood or body fluids contaminated with blood.

rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis-B clinical and public-health management
rows.verified: UKHSA surveillance monitors acute and chronic hepatitis B trends and population inequalities.

rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis-B clinical and public-health management
rows.verified: Laboratory reports are a primary source for national hepatitis-B surveillance.

rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis-B clinical and public-health management
rows.verified: Healthcare-worker guidance covers health clearance and management for workers living with bloodborne viruses.

rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis-B clinical and public-health management
rows.verified: Hepatitis-B risk depends on vaccination, exposure route, viral load, contact type, host factors, setting and follow-up timing.

rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis-B clinical and public-health management
rows.verified: UKHSA hepatitis-B evidence is patient-, exposure-, laboratory-, vaccination-, care- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.

rows.source: OPSS baby self-feeding product safety
rows.verified: OPSS classifies baby self-feeding products as presenting a serious risk of harm or death.

rows.source: OPSS baby self-feeding product safety
rows.verified: These products can create choking risk by allowing feed to flow without caregiver control.

rows.source: OPSS baby self-feeding product safety
rows.verified: They can also create a risk of aspiration pneumonia.

rows.source: OPSS baby self-feeding product safety
rows.verified: OPSS states that the risk arises from the product design and intended use.

rows.source: OPSS baby self-feeding product safety
rows.verified: Instructions or supervision cannot make the category safe according to the alert.

rows.source: OPSS baby self-feeding product safety
rows.verified: Consumers are advised to stop using the products immediately and dispose of them safely.

rows.source: OPSS baby self-feeding product safety
rows.verified: Businesses are required to remove these products from the market.

rows.source: OPSS baby self-feeding product safety
rows.verified: Recent recalls show that self-feeding pillows continue to be identified and removed from sale.

rows.source: OPSS baby self-feeding product safety
rows.verified: Self-feeding-product risk depends on design, flow rate, infant position, age, caregiver control, product condition and response time.

rows.source: OPSS baby self-feeding product safety
rows.verified: OPSS self-feeding evidence is product-, design-, infant-, use-, clinical- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level choking probability.
